title: NSUI and student groups protest in Bengaluru demanding CEC's resignation

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.
tea.want: Demonstrators are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the scrapping of the SIR process.
tea.changed: Oct 10: Police detained student demonstrators at Freedom Park while they attempted to march toward the Election Commission office.

summary: Members of the National Students' Union of India and other student organizations staged demonstrations in Bengaluru, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The protests were sparked by allegations of irregularities surrounding the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. The agitation began on October 6 with an NSUI protest, and continued on October 10 when student groups attempted to march toward the Election Commission office from Freedom Park amid heavy security. Organisers stated the demonstration involved groups such as the NSUI, AISA, SFI, AIDSO, and AISF. Authorities deployed heavy police personnel, barricaded the area, and detained protesters who tried to bypass the barriers. Organising bodies condemned the police action as a suppression of democratic rights and called for the immediate release of those taken into custody.
demands: Resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar
Scrapping of the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls
Upholding transparency, fairness, and accountability in the Election Commission
Protection of every eligible citizen's right to vote
Immediate release of detained protesters and removal of barricades
response: Police deployed heavy personnel, barricaded roads around Freedom Park, and detained protesters when they attempted to march toward the Election Commission office.

updates.text: NSUI Karnataka staged a protest in Bengaluru demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
Student organisation members gathered at Freedom Park and were detained while attempting to march to the EC office.
